jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Digitalization
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for one or more vacant Assistant Professorship (s) in Information Systems and Digitalization at the Department of Digitalization.

CBS is a globally recognized business school with a robust interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment. The Department of Digitalization is an engaged and diverse community of scholars exploring the interplay between technology and organizations, with impact-driven research and teaching at its core. Our main research areas include (but not exclusively):

1. Business intelligence and data science

2. Data studies

3. Digital ecosystem and sustainability

4. Digital government

5. IT management and enterprise architecture

6. Hybrid threats and defence tech

7. Digital transformation of work and society

We prioritize high-quality research and are committed to publishing in leading academic journals, with a particular focus on the AIS premier journal list (https://aisnet.org/research/seniorscholarsbasket/ ).

Teaching responsibilities of the department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching in Digitalization, please read more about our programmes: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/departments-and-centres/ department-of-digitalization/ degree-programmes

We are interested in candidates with a PhD in Information Systems and Digitalization, ideally with a strong technical background (e.g., MSc in Computer Science, Data Science, or related fields).

Candidates are expected to have a promising research pipeline and a commitment to contribute to advancing scholarship in the fields of information systems and digitalization.

We are particularly interested in candidates who can teach following subjects:

• 
Data science, Artificial Intelligence, and their mathematical and computational foundations (e.g., linear algebra, machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing)

• 
Cyber security

• 
Enterprise architecture

The assistant professorship is a tenure track position (6 years) with research and teaching obligations.

To fulfil the research requirements of the position, the applicant(s) chosen is expected to be physically present on a regular basis and actively participate in the teaching and research activities of the Department. The successful applicant is obliged to participate in the assistant professor program at CBS on teaching principles and methods in order to fulfil the pedagogical requirements made at the end of the term of employment as assistant professor.

Responsibilities 

• 
Teaching and associated examination in existing CBS programs, including Executive Education

• 
Individual and group based research meeting high international standards

• 
Promoting CBS’s academic reputation

• 
Initiating, fund raising and coordinating research projects

• 
Promoting the teaching and research capabilities of Copenhagen Business School and other relevant assignments at Copenhagen Business School

• 
Contributing to the administrative responsibilities of the department and to CBS-wide tasks

• 
Communicating findings to the public in general and to CBS’s stakeholders in particular

• 
Research, including responsibility for the academic development of the relevant discipline

• 
Responsibility for publishing, scientific communication and research-based teaching

• 
Active participation in the regular research activities, such as research seminars, workshops and conferences.

The assistant professor is expected to contribute to the development and application of the research of the department’s research areas and to maintain and strengthen CBS’s international research position. 

Qualification 

The applicant must hold a PhD or the equivalent. Emphasis is placed on the applicant’s research potential, which means that a researcher with a large research potential may be preferred to a researcher with a large research production. 

The applicant must have professional proficiency in English (written and spoken). 

Copenhagen Business School has a broad commitment to the excellence, distinctiveness and relevance of its teaching and research programmes. Candidates who wish to join us should demonstrate enthusiasm for working in an organisation of this type.

For further information please contact: Head of Department Andrea Carugati via e-mail ac.digi@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/digi.

Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organisation.

Application 

Application must be sent via the electronic recruitment system.

Application must include: 

• 
A statement of application.

• 
Proof of qualifications and a full CV.

• 
Documentation of relevant, significant, original research at an international level, including publications in the field’s internationally recognized journals and citations in the Social Science Citation Index and/or Google Scholar.

• 
A teaching portfolio documenting teaching qualifications and pedagogical development. The portfolio must include an overview of the applicants past teaching achievements and practice and its impact on the students, reflections on pedagogical competencies and core strengths, the educational competencies the applicant would like to develop, and the teaching opportunities they would like to pursue in the nearest future. External applicants can see the full description of the teaching portfolio here. Internal applicants must use the CBS Teaching Portfolio format. It is available at www.share.cbs.dk. Please make a pdf of each of the spreadsheets from part B of the portfolio.

• 
Information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation and international co-operation.

• 
A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 10 publications for review are allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.

• 
Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration.

Recruitment procedure 

The Recruitment Committee will shortlist minimum two applicants; when possible five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline.

The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Would you like to work with financial regulation and compliance while contributing to the development of a growing regulatory services business at Netcompany Banking Services?

As a Business Consultant, you will work with compliance and risk management while supporting legal and governance matters for financial institutions. You will combine your regulatory expertise with an analytical and structured approach to help our customers navigate complex regulatory requirements and strengthen their compliance and risk frameworks.

We are currently expanding our regulatory services offering, where you will play an important role in delivering and further developing our services to financial institutions. Our services within the compliance and risk areas cover the regulatory process from monitoring legislation and assessing compliance risks to annual planning, data-supported compliance reviews and regulatory reporting.

We focus on the use of automation and new technologies to develop efficient and scalable regulatory services. Working closely with colleagues across data and technology, you will contribute to high-quality customer deliveries and the continued development of regulatory Services.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

As a Business Consultant, you will support the Head of Regulatory Banking Services in delivering high-quality regulatory services to financial institutions. You will contribute to daily customer deliveries while helping to develop and standardise processes, control frameworks and reporting models.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• 
Prepare and maintain compliance risk assessments and annual compliance plans for financial clients.

• 
Develop control frameworks, control questions and supporting documentation, including reviewing and quality-assuring data and control results.

• 
Prepare compliance review reports, quarterly and annual reports, and follow up on identified risks, observations and recommendations.

• 
Monitor and assess relevant financial regulation and contribute to translating regulatory requirements into control activities, policies, procedures and governance documentation.

• 
Contribute to the development of regulatory services, including supporting risk management activities and collaborating with data and technology specialists to improve and automate processes.

About you

We imagine that you have:

• 
A relevant academic degree, such as law, business law or a related field, combined with around 2–5 years of experience in compliance, financial regulation or similar areas.

• 
Solid knowledge of financial regulation and preferably experience from a compliance function within a financial institution, ideally in the second line of defence.

• 
Practical experience with regulatory risk assessments, control frameworks, documentation and compliance reporting. Experience with risk management is an advantage.

• 
Strong analytical and communication skills, a structured approach to your work and an interest in data, technology and the digitalisation of regulatory processes.

• 
Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must. Your day-to-day working environment will, however, primarily be Danish-speaking.

Join an inclusive community

We highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

Send us an application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

A property manager can handle 600 tenants. That's the industry limit. Why? Because the work scales linearly: matching bank transactions to invoices, chasing late payments, answering tenant questions, coordinating repairs, preparing legal notices, renewing leases. More tenants, more of the same manual work.

With AI, that limit disappears. And both landlords and tenants get a better experience.

**About Rumli

**Eight years in property operations. ~1,000 customers across Denmark, the Netherlands, and Germany. We know this industry: the workflows, the pain points, the regulations.

Now we're making a big move: becoming a property manager. Tenant communication, bookkeeping, coordinating repairs. We handle it all. A landlord shouldn't chase late payments or find a plumber at 10 pm. We do it for them.

We're building an entirely new platform to power this. AI-native from day one. Profitable, real customers, expanding across the Nordics.

**Why this is interesting

**Property management is a great domain for a product engineer. Thousands of similar transactions, pattern-based decisions, templated documents. And 1,000 customers who will tell you exactly where it hurts. Years of domain knowledge, ready to turn into a product.

We ship with AI agents built into the workflow. Our codebase has custom skills to improve our workflow. AI writes a lot of the code; we review it. That means the slow part of building isn't writing code anymore. It's knowing what to build. That's what this role is about.

**The role

**You are autonomous and independent, working with the team to solve property managers' pains and make them as efficient as possible.

• Talk to customers and property managers. Find out what actually slows them down

• Decide what to build, then build it. Mockup, prototype, ship, measure, repeat

• Own features end-to-end. Database to API to UI

• Build AI into core product features

• Work directly with our co-founder on product direction

We need someone who looks at a messy problem and figures out what to build, and doesn't wait for a spec.

**Tech stack

**TypeScript everywhere. But does it even matter anymore?

• Frontend: Next.js, React, Shadcn, Tailwind CSS

• Backend: NestJS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM

• Infra: AWS Lambda, CDK, RDS, EventBridge, SQS

**What We're Looking For

**

• Product thinking. You understand what it takes to build a profitable product. You are not here just to handle tickets.

• Strong product mindset. Agents can code, but they need scoping and steering.

• You've shipped things people actually use, and you can show them.

• Comfortable talking to customers.

• Experience with coding agents.

• Work independently.

• Copenhagen-based (on-site).

Big plus: AWS, AI experience (prompt engineering, RAG, agents), fintech/proptech background, a side project you're proud of.

**Compensation & Benefits

**

• Compensation: 50–65K DKK, depending on experience and demonstrated competencies

• Equity: Employee warrants offering real ownership in the company

• Workspace: Centrally located Copenhagen office

• Perks: Daily lunch included

**Why Rumli?

**Real customers. Brand-new codebase. Small team where your decisions matter.

We're rebuilding from the ground up with AI as the foundation. If you want to decide what property software should do, not just build what someone else specified, reach out.

**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered. If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**Portfolio Analysis is where investment professionals turn data into insight on portfolios, performance and risk. Our products are business critical and widely used, so they need to keep evolving in a responsible way. Right now that means strong maintainability, high system performance, mature CI/CD, and reshaping parts of SimCorp Dimension for the cloud.

As a Senior Software Engineer in our Product Division, you will join an agile team of 5–7 people in the Portfolio Analysis Product Area. You will mainly work on backend components, APIs and services, using C#, .NET, Dyalog APL and Oracle.

AI is part of how we work every day. We see it as a natural part of modern software engineering, alongside source control, testing, CI/CD and code reviews. AI does not replace engineering judgment. It helps good engineers learn faster, reduce repetitive work and build better software.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Understand and challenge customer requirements together with your team, then design, implement, test and support the chosen solutions

• Design, develop and maintain backend functionality and APIs using C# and .NET, and work with Dyalog APL where it is part of the product

• Contribute to cloud modernization and scalable service design where it adds real value

• Improve performance, maintainability, testability and developer experience

• Take ownership beyond code: contribute to design discussions and help the team make sound technical decisions

• Use CI/CD, automated testing and code reviews as natural parts of daily engineering work

• Use AI every day in practical engineering work, such as exploring ideas, understanding unfamiliar code, prototyping, improving tests, documenting decisions and automating routine tasks

• Help the team discover where AI creates real value and where traditional engineering judgment should lead

• Collaborate with product owners, domain experts and fellow engineers to turn customer needs into good software

**What We Value

**How you gained your skills matters less than your ability to learn, collaborate and take ownership. We expect you to know some of the following and to be interested in learning the rest:

• C# and .NET development, backend development and API design

• Building high-performance, scalable and maintainable applications

• Continuous integration and delivery, automated testing and practical quality engineering

• Relational databases, preferably Oracle or similar

• Cloud technologies, distributed systems or Azure-based services

• Willingness to learn additional technologies, including Dyalog APL

• Curiosity about AI-assisted software engineering and daily use of modern tools

• Experience with financial instruments or investment systems is an advantage but not a requirement. We will bring you up to speed through training and a comprehensive onboarding program.

We also value people who take ownership and deliver results. We look for engineers who try new approaches, work with others to leverage everyone’s strengths, and balance technical quality with business value. We want you to help build an inclusive, trust-based engineering culture.

**Benefits

**

• Global hybrid work policy – We ask you to work 2 days a week from the office. You can work remotely the other days if you choose.

• Growth and innovation – Every sixth sprint is reserved for planning, innovation, learning and improvements.

• Self-direction – Teams and developers have a high degree of freedom to plan, organize and design their work.

• Modern engineering in a real product context – You will work on cloud modernization, AI-enabled development and performance in large-scale financial software.

• Inclusive and diverse company culture – We want people to bring different perspectives and contribute to a respectful workplace.

• Work-life balance – We believe balance between professional and private life makes us better colleagues and better engineers.

• Empowerment – All voices are valuable, and you will be involved in shaping our work processes.

**NEXT STEPS

Help build how AI is done right in a medical device company

Imagine joining a team at the very beginning. Not to maintain something others designed, but to shape what it becomes: the code, the platform, the way of working and the people around you. That is the opportunity in our Quality AI Enabler team.

We are a small team working where AI, cloud technology, software engineering, data and Quality meet. Together with our AI Business Analyst and Quality Engineering Graduate, you will turn promising AI ideas and prototypes into secure, maintainable solutions that help our Quality colleagues work smarter, and ultimately support the quality of the hearing aids that improve people's lives every day. You will be the team's engineering anchor, and with that comes real influence on what we build and how we build it.

Your days will be hands-on. You will design, build and deploy AI-assisted workflows and applications in Microsoft Azure, using large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, AI agents, and enterprise data. You will write backend services, APIs and integrations, and you know what it takes to move a prototype into production. You probably have around 4-6 years of software development behind you, and you have already shipped something real with generative AI.

But this role is about more than code. You will set the engineering practices the team grows on, create reusable patterns for future AI initiatives, and help less experienced colleagues grow through pairing, reviews and sharing what you know. You do not need a manager title to lead: you lead by example, explain technical choices in plain language, and challenge assumptions when something looks fragile.

And then there are the guardrails. Hearing aids are regulated medical devices, so in our company responsible AI is not a slide in a presentation; it is part of the design. You will help define how we handle security, data access, evaluation and AI lifecycle controls, and you will learn how the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 13485 and IEC 62304 shape what good looks like. Experience from a regulated industry is an advantage, but curiosity matters more. Few places let you build this knowledge from the ground up. We are one such place.

What you bring

• Strong development skills in Python or another language

• Hands-on experience deploying solutions in Microsoft Azure

• Practical experience with generative AI and LLM-based applications

• Working knowledge of REST APIs, MCP servers or similar integrations

• Git, automated testing and CI/CD as daily habits

• A solid grasp of authentication, secrets and application security

• Clear communication in English

Pharma communication is slow for a good reason. Every claim needs a reference, every asset needs approval, and every market has its own rules. We think the software that wins in this industry treats those rules as part of the product rather than something to work around, and that is what we build.

Anthill builds the software pharmaceutical companies use to create, approve and run their digital communication. At some of the world's largest pharma companies, commercial and medical teams rely on our products to produce and distribute regulated content. We're around 70 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, with four products: Activator, Arcane, Amplify and Anthill Cloud. Our products are already delivering GenAI-powered capabilities to Enterprise customers around the world.

We're growing fast, and it's a good time to join. In our Copenhagen office, engineers, designers, product people and strategists all sit in the same room. We're 15+ nationalities, so English is the official and everyday language in the office and in the codebase.

We are hiring a software engineer into our backend chapter.

What you will actually work on

Anthill Cloud is the shared platform layer behind our products. It handles identity, tenancy, content and the services that belong across the suite rather than inside any one product. Most of the interesting backend work at Anthill over the next two years sits on that line: deciding what belongs to a product, what belongs to the platform, and how to move something from one to the other without breaking a client who is mid-campaign.

We run on AWS. Lambda, ECS, API Gateway, EventBridge, DynamoDB, RDS, S3 and CloudWatch, with Terraform as how infrastructure gets changed. The code is Node: TypeScript on NestJS for Anthill Cloud, and JavaScript in parts of the product backends.

Coding agents write a growing share of that code, which moves most of the engineering to the work around it: shaping the solution, running spikes before anyone commits to an approach, building the harness agents work inside, orchestrating the work, and judging what comes back. You still write the code yourself when that is the better way.

In your first year you will:

• Shape solutions before they are built: service boundaries, contracts and data models, written down as decision records in the repo that people and agents build from.

• Run spikes that answer a technical question with evidence before a mission commits to an approach, and throw the spike away once it has.

• Build the harness our agents work inside: the specs, agent instructions, tests and checks that keep generated code inside the architecture, and tighten it when something gets through.

• Orchestrate agent work on changes that span several services: split it so agents can do it well, and own how the pieces fit together.

• Build and run services on Anthill Cloud, serverless or containerised depending on what the workload actually needs.

• Turn product-level capability into shared services the rest of the suite can call, including the unglamorous part where you migrate the original caller.

• Build integrations into the systems our clients already run, including Veeva, DAM platforms and client identity providers. Pharma clients do not adopt tools that ignore their existing stack.

• Work on the data models behind content authoring, modular content and referencing. The domain has real structure to it and getting the model wrong is expensive.

• Run what you build. You will have production access, you will see your own service misbehave, and you will fix it.

The levels

We are hiring at mid or senior level and will fit the role to the person we meet. The kind of work is the same at both. What changes is scope. A mid owns features and the design inside them, and works well inside service boundaries and agent setups that someone else defined. A senior owns decisions that outlast the mission they were made in, and other engineers and agents build on them. Tell us where you think you sit, and we will tell you if we see it differently. You do not need to tick every box below. Some of this is learned here.

What we are looking for

• Backend development against cloud services, ideally AWS.

• JavaScript, TypeScript and Node you can write well yourself, without an agent.

• Hands-on work with databases, both SQL and NoSQL.

• Infrastructure as code. We use Terraform.

• CI/CD pipelines, and some appetite for the operational side of what you ship.

• API design for consumers you do not control, and the discipline that comes with not being able to change them at will.

• Solution design you have done yourself and lived with: service boundaries, contracts and data models, written clearly enough that an engineer or an agent can build from it, including the decisions you would now make differently.

• Spikes and prototypes that answered a question rather than became the product, and the discipline to throw them away.

• Experience with agent-driven development: daily work with coding agents such as Claude Code, building the context, instructions and checks they work inside, splitting work so they can do it well, reviewing what comes back to the standard you would hold a colleague to, and knowing when to stop and write it yourself.

• Working English. Danish is not required.

Useful, not required:

• NestJS and TypeORM, or another structured Node framework.

• Event-driven architecture, and experience with the failure modes rather than the diagrams.

• Python or another backend language alongside Node.

• Experience in a regulated industry: GxP, validated systems, ISO 27001, or anything where an auditor eventually reads your change log.

• Work on AI features in production, including retrieval and evaluation. We run on AWS Bedrock and have a dedicated AI chapter you would work alongside.

• Agent tooling you have built yourself: MCP servers, agent instructions shared across a team, or evaluations of what agents produce.

How we work

Engineers belong to a chapter and work in missions. The chapter is your professional home and where your craft is developed.

Missions are time boxed, cross functional teams pointed at one outcome. When a round of missions closes, people rotate and a new set forms. The rotation is the point. Over a couple of years you work with most of the engineering team and across most of the product surface, instead of spending three years in one squad on one corner of the codebase.

Product decisions run through HIVE, our gate model. Nothing gets built because someone senior liked the idea. Initiatives pass through evidence, solution framing and a funding decision before engineering starts, and they are not closed until the outcome is validated rather than when the code ships. As an engineer this means you get told why something is being built, and you are expected to argue if the reasoning is thin.

What is agreed gets written down in the repo, as docs and decision records that people and coding agents both work from. A growing share of the engineering is in that writing and in the review, rather than in typing the code.

We work trunk based on Anthill Cloud and review each other's code, including the code our agents write. We expect the person who merges something to be able to explain how it runs, and we hold the line on security and access because our clients audit us and we hold their data.

What we offer

• A permanent Danish employment contract, pension and health insurance.

• A salary set from our salary bands, the same way for everyone at the same level. Where you land in the range depends on your experience and skills, and on pay equity with colleagues at that level.

• Five days a week in our Copenhagen office, with two work from home days a month as the default. We are on site because most of what engineers learn from each other happens in conversation at someone's desk.

• Colleagues who have shipped software into pharma and know how demanding that audience is.

• Clients whose problems are specific and constrained, which is more interesting than it sounds.

• Occasional office dogs, who expect to be petted.

In the interview you use the tools you use at work, coding agents included. You will also write some code without one, review code an agent wrote and tell us what is wrong with it, and take a design problem from question to plan with us: how you would shape the service, what you would spike first, and how you would set agents up to build it.

Sebastian Søberg leads the backend chapter and would be your manager. He is also our Senior Solution Architect and the person you argue with about architecture, which we consider a feature. Questions about the role can go to him on LinkedIn.

You will help make the architectural decisions at the platform layer, not be handed the result of them.

Applying

If you can recognise yourself in just some of these requirements or skills and simply want to learn the rest, we would love to receive your application. We offer an open environment with freedom under responsibility, where you have the opportunity to grow professionally.

Apply through LinkedIn, or get in touch directly if you would rather have a conversation before a formal application. We read everything ourselves.

Your CV does not need a photo, your age or anything else that is not about your work.

If there is a repository, a component library, a test plan, a bug report you are proud of, a design document or a postmortem that tells us more than a cover letter would, send that too.

We review applications as they arrive. Where the role has a closing date, it is stated at the top of the ad. Otherwise the role stays open until we find the right person.

We only work with recruitment and search firms under a written agreement, and we do not pay fees for candidates we did not ask for. Please do not send CVs to the hiring manager.

Your role

As Senior Business Change & Execution Lead, you will run the business-side change and delivery engine that turns strategy into outcomes. Working closely with the Head of Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence, our Business Process Owners, Global IT, and implementation partners, you will ensure that governance runs, decisions move forward, markets are ready, and change lands - wave by wave during rollout, and release by release after go-live. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Owning the business readiness and adoption roadmap across markets and rollout waves, covering milestones, risks and dependencies, aligned with Global IT's project plan.

• Driving change execution: readiness diagnostics, stakeholder mapping, communication and enablement plans, adoption tracking, and go-live preparation.

• Running the governance cadence, including Core Team and delegate forums, and preparing SteerCo decision material, with clear agendas, decision logs and follow-up.

• Leading regular touchpoints with market Business Leads, and coordinating across Global IT, implementation partners, platform vendors, regional teams and local markets.

• Creating executive materials, stakeholder communications, briefing packs and change narratives that reflect LEO Pharma's business context.

• After go-live: running the roadmap prioritisation process with Business Process Owners, and tracking adoption and business value so the platform keeps delivering.

You will also help ensure that learnings are captured and acted on throughout the implementation, so the approach improves wave by wave. This is not a passive coordination role — you will bring structure, recommendations, momentum, and follow-through.

Your qualifications

We imagine that you bring strong experience from complex business change, adoption, transformation, or global implementation environments. You know how to make change work in practice - not only how to design the framework.

We are especially looking for:

• Proven experience leading business change and adoption in large-scale, multi-market implementations.

• Hands-on experience with structured change methods such as ADKAR or equivalent; Prosci certification is a plus.

• Strong execution skills, including roadmaps, RAID, governance, delivery cadence, and readiness tracking.

• Experience defining and tracking adoption and business value metrics, and using them to drive prioritisation.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, including senior stakeholder and executive-level materials.

• Experience working with external implementation partners, platform vendors, and cross-functional global teams.

Experience from pharma, life sciences commercial operations, CRM platform implementation (such as Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud or Veeva), Agile delivery, or train-the-trainer models will be an advantage.

As a person, you are structured, persistent, and action-oriented. You simplify complexity, create momentum, and bring a clear point of view on what needs to happen next. You lead through influence rather than hierarchy - holding partners, process owners, and markets to their commitments while bringing people with you. You keep the end user in mind — because change that does not work for the field, the medical liaison, or the market team does not work at all.

What success looks like

About C-Leanship

C-Leanship is a Danish cleantech company delivering underwater inspection, hull cleaning, propeller cleaning and niche area cleaning to the global shipping industry. Our ShipShiner ROV system for hull cleaning works on a zero-discharge model. Removed fouling is captured rather than released into the port, so vessels can be cleaned in terminal and at anchorage during normal port operations without disrupting schedules. Our NCPS Propeller Cleaner cleans propellers alongside the terminal, with no need to shift to anchorage.

We have built a strong position in the container segment. Now we are entering our next growth phase. We are taking our services into the wider shipping market, with bulk carriers and tankers as key segments, and expanding our network of service hubs to serve more of the world’s major ports.

We are headquartered in Køge, Denmark, and operate service hubs in Singapore, Busan and Panama. We work with leading shipowners, vessel operators and vessel paint manufacturers. We are backed by Saab Ventures, Wallenius and EnvisionTech.

The role

We are looking for an experienced sales professional, a hunter, to win new international customers, grow our markets and secure new framework agreements. As Senior Sales Manager you will be one of the most senior commercial voices in C-Leanship. You will own a defined territory and a set of strategic accounts. You will open new international customers and convert first jobs into framework agreements that deliver recurring revenue.

You sell on value. You translate regular and correct cleaning into what our customers measure: fuel cost, CII rating, regulatory compliance and the lifetime of the coating system. You do this credibly with every stakeholder, from Superintendent and Performance Manager to Head of Fuel Efficiency, Technical Director and C-level.

You report to our Chief Commercial Officer, Lasse Urth. You will work closely with Operations and Operational Excellence to make sure that what we sell is delivered to standard. Through your own way of working, you will help set the standard for how C-Leanship sells and raise the bar for the wider sales team.

What you will own

• Track regulation, market trends and competitor activity across the ROV and maritime sector, including IMO biofouling guidelines, CII and port requirements, and turn that insight into territory plans

• Contribute to the commercial strategy and represent C-Leanship at customer meetings, industry events and exhibitions

What success looks like

• First 30 days: full command of our services, technology and customer base. Key relationships are established across your portfolio, with close working ties to Operations and the sales teams in Denmark, Singapore and Korea.

• By month three: your first cleaning deals are closed in your own name. Your pipeline is built, growing, qualified and visible in HubSpot, and you have a clear plan and stakeholder map for your first framework agreement.

• By month twelve: your first framework agreement is signed. Customers recognise you as a trusted advisor on biofouling management and vessel performance. You are an active voice in our commercial strategy and a visible benchmark for how we sell.

What we are looking for

• At least 7 years of international B2B sales experience, including at least 3 consecutive years in solution or value-based sales within the maritime or shipping industry

• A proven track record of winning spot deals and initial business, ideally with shipowners, operators or ship managers, and turning them into recurring business through framework agreements or long-term service contracts

• Commercially sharp and results-oriented, with a high and sustained sales drive

• A credible communicator who adapts style and argument to each stakeholder

• Analytical and data-driven, comfortable building a business case on fuel and emissions data

• A start-up mindset: hands-on, robust and comfortable with change, with the energy to build from scratch and thrive in a fast-growing company

Nice to have

Why this role is different

This is a senior, visible commercial role in a scaling cleantech company. You will have direct access to the management team and real influence on how we grow. You will sell a technology with a measurable impact on fuel cost, emissions and ocean health, in an international environment spanning Denmark, Singapore, Korea and Panama. We offer a competitive salary and commission package that reflects your seniority and experience.

Where you will work

Køge, Denmark, our HQ, or Singapore, our Asia Pacific base. The role is full-time and permanent, with around 10–20 travel days a year.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short motivation to our Chief Commercial Officer, Lasse Urth, at lur@c-leanship.com. For questions about the position, please contact Lasse as well. We review applications on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

**About Sedna:

**Sedna is at the forefront of revolutionising the operating system for shipping. Our AI-powered platform is designed to make global trade more efficient, transparent, and sustainable. As we continue to grow and innovate, we are looking for exceptional talent to join our journey and contribute to our mission of transforming the shipping industry .

You can find out more about us on our website: https://sedna.com/

**About the role

**This role focuses on contributing to the design, development, and evolution of Sedna’s VMS (Voyage Management System). It's a mature, highly specialised platform that shipowners, operators and charterers use to run chartering, voyage operations, cargo and freight/hire invoicing.

VMS has a Java backend exposing a REST API used by our own web client (React) and directly by customers' integrations. Data lives in Oracle, including a significant amount of business logic in PL/SQL. It runs on AWS and builds through GitLab CI/CD.

Sedna VMS is in use 24/7 by shipping companies worldwide. Customers run their daily operations and invoicing on it, so correctness, performance and reliability directly affect their business.

You will play a key part in raising standards and delivering new features. You'll take real ownership of features and of how they behave in production, on a product customers run their business on, and help shape how the platform evolves. You'll work with modern AI-assisted development tools as part of everyday engineering.

**How you’ll make an impact

****Engineering and feature development

**This role contributes to both backend and frontend development. Day-to-day responsibilities include understanding requirements, shaping technical approaches, writing code, and contributing to automated tests. Development work spans a mix of new features, improvements, and maintenance, driven by both customer and product needs.

**System architecture and modernisation

**The role includes participating in ongoing efforts to refine and modernise the platform. This involves contributing to technical upgrade work, improving system structure, and supporting longer-term architectural direction as the product grows. Opportunities exist to participate in design discussions and help shape solutions that improve system performance, reliability, and extensibility.

**Quality, testing, and delivery practices

**The team maintains a focus on software quality. We combine unit tests, API regression tests (Postman) and UI tests (Playwright) with peer code review on every merge request. Releases are built and tested through GitLab CI/CD. We're actively improving here: getting more of our test suites running automatically in CI and making them reliable. Engineers who want to drive that, will have room to do it.

**Collaboration with product and customer-facing teams

**The role involves close collaboration with product managers through refinement, planning, and solution discussions. Engineers also interact with Customer Support on cases that need engineering input, and, for larger projects, join customer conversations to validate technical approaches.

**Continuous improvement and documentation

**We treat documentation, including API references, design decisions and runbooks, as part of delivering a change. Much of VMS's knowledge still sits with experienced team members, and capturing it in written, searchable form is an active priority. We also reserve time for technical debt and internal improvements.

**In your first 90 days, you can expect

**

• Month 1: Build your understanding of Sedna’s architecture and our products. Get set up with the VMS codebase, your dev environment and the release process, and ship your first changes. Meet your team, product manager and key customer-facing colleagues. Learn the maritime workflows our customers depend on.

• Month 2: Take ownership of a well-scoped piece of work from refinement with product through to release. Contribute to design discussions, give timely and constructive code review feedback. Shadow the on-call rotation and get familiar with runbooks and production tooling.

• Month 3: Lead the technical approach on a complex feature or improvement within your team, working independently and raising risks and dependencies early. Join the on-call rotation. Contribute improvements to tests, runbooks or documentation based on what you found hard to learn, and support technical validation in a customer conversation where relevant.

**What we're looking for:

****Essential experience

**Candidates typically bring three+ years of professional engineering experience from a comparable environment. Experience working on production systems where quality and reliability are important. Familiarity with a JVM language (Java, Kotlin, Scala) or a similar backend language, React or another modern frontend framework. Strong SQL and relational database skills, ideally Oracle or PostgreSQL, including query performance. Experience supporting production systems: diagnosing incidents from logs and metrics. Prior on-call experience is a plus.

**Critical skills

**A strong grasp of building and maintaining features within a larger system is helpful. Confidence with automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and code review workflows is expected. Clear thinking, good problem-solving ability, and the capacity to work with domain-heavy logic contribute to success in the role. Experience with enterprise or workflow-driven applications is an advantage.

**Traits and mindset

**Curiosity and a willingness to learn the maritime domain are appreciated. A collaborative working style, comfort sharing ideas in cross-functional settings, and the ability to work independently when needed all support strong performance. Adaptability is important as the product and architecture continue to evolve.

**Core competencies

**Systems thinking, ownership of outcomes, strong communication skills, and effective collaboration are central to this role. A motivation to create value for customers and contribute to a stable, evolving platform is essential.

**What’s In Store for You

**

• A strong team. You’ll join a global team of senior and staff engineers who set a high bar and will help level you up.

• A generous salary and benefits package (depending on experience) + private medical, equity, health and wellbeing benefits, home internet contribution

• Scalability challenges. You’ll be a part of evolving our VMS system as we further develop in to a product led company.

• Customer impact. Real customers use our products everyday, you'll see your work impacting real people.

• Collaboration & autonomy. Plenty of heads-down technical work, but also close partnership with product engineers and engineering leadership.

**Our Values:

**Finally, culture is important to us, so we also look for candidates who share our values:

**Stay Ahead, Stay Agile

**

• We don’t just adapt-we anticipate change and act with confidence.

• Curiosity, data, and customer insights help us stay ahead of the curve.

• We embrace challenges as opportunities and remain resilient under pressure.

• By staying open to new ideas and ways of working, we lead the future.

**Execute With Focus

**

• We turn strategy into action, delivering measurable results that matter.

• Every initiative counts-discipline and ownership drive business impact.

• We make smart decisions with speed, balancing pace and precision.

• Clear priorities keep us focused on what moves the needle.

**Work Together, Win Together

**

• Collaboration is our superpower-we succeed as one team, internally and with customers.

• We co-create solutions, seek feedback, and build the future of Sedna together.

• Strong relationships are built on trust, respect, and shared goals.

• By aligning across teams and with customers, we unlock greater impact.

Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

  Within the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA), University of Copenhagen is offering a 1-year Research Assistant (RA) position starting 1 April 2027 (or as soon as possible thereafter), which then leads to a 3-year PhD fellowship for a Doctoral Candidate (DC).

  The combined position is part of the research project STEP-UP (Safe, Thriving, and Engaged Pedestrians in Urban Public Spaces), which is funded by the European Union’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA), Doctoral Networks (DN), Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01.

  The STEP-UP network supports 10 PhD Candidates in investigating pedestrian behaviour and mobility in urban environments.

  The 10 PhD projects are closely linked, contributing complementary perspectives to a shared research agenda in three areas: individual and interpersonal aspects of pedestrian behaviour, environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking, and interactions between pedestrians and other road users. The aim is to improve the understanding of pedestrian mobility and support the development of safer and more inclusive urban public spaces.

  STEP-UP brings together academic and non-academic partners to train 10 doctoral candidates through an international Joint Doctorate programme. The candidates benefit from joint supervision by researchers at partner institutions, an integrated doctoral training programme, and opportunities for interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration, including research secondments at partner organisations. In addition to specialised scientific knowledge, they develop transferable skills in areas such as research communication and dissemination. The programme prepares them for careers in research and other fields related to transport and urban development.

  For a description of the STEP-UP project and descriptions of all 10 PhD positions, please visit the STEP-UP project’s website https://www.project-stepup.eu/

  STEP-UP is based on 4-year double PhD degree programs. This means that the successful applicant will also be enrolled in a partner university’s PhD programme.

  Job and project description
 The RA position will entail carrying out a literature review of the research field, identifying current research gaps, and preparing for data collection. 

  The PhD position will entail carrying out the research activities of the research project as described below.

  Your key tasks as a PhD fellow at the Faculty of SCIENCE are to:

   	
• Conduct an independent research project under supervision. 	
• Complete PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participate in active research environments including a mandatory stay for a minimum of 12 months at the partner university (see below for further details). 	
• Contribute to teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project (e.g., at conferences, meetings, etc.) 	
• Write a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   About the research project
 The project “Urban space transformation projects for improved and inclusive walkability”. will investigate how planning and design approaches applied in urban space transformation projects impact pedestrians’ behaviour and perceived safety and accessibility (walkability). Urban transformation projects are increasingly proposed to respond to the evolving needs of contemporary cities. Combining urban planning and transport engineering is essential, as planning shapes the spatial and social context of urban spaces while transport engineering ensures safe, efficient and accessible movement. The PhD project will:  (1) collect data on goals and practices of urban space transformation projects; pedestrian pedestrians’ behaviours, preferences and perceptions of walkability in relation to the transformation interventions; (2) identify walkability indicators across diverse groups of pedestrians; (3) comprehensively evaluate pedestrians’ perceived impacts of current transformations for enhanced liveability and pedestrianisation; and (4) develop a methodological framework for local adaptation and upscaling of approaches for enhanced perceived walkability. Partner university: National Technical University of Athens (NTUA) Planned secondments at NTUA: M16–M24 and M37–M48.

  Pricipal supervisor: Assoc. Prof. Trine Agervig Carstensen, University of Copenhagen, email: tac@ign.ku.dk.

  Co-supervisor: Prof. Konstantinos Kepaptsoglou, National Technical University of Athens (NTUA), email: kkepap@central.ntua.gr

  Place of employment
 The primary place of employment will be Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state-of-the-art hardware and software. More information on the department can be found here: https://ign.ku.dk/english/

  During the PhD programme of research the candidate will be on a secondment for minimum 12 months in total at the partner university.

  Required qualifications
 As an applicant you must have:

   	
• To be eligible for the PhD programme at UCPH, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Urban Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Psychology, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Sociology, or related-disciplines. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 	
• To be eligible for the PhD programme at the National University of Athens, you are required to fulfil the requirements described here: https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.survey.ntua.gr%2Fen%2Fstudies%2Fpostgraduate%2Fdoctoral-studies&data=05%7C02%7Ctac%40ign.ku.dk%7Ce197702553f44a00a12308df44a25d10%7Ca3927f91cda14696af898c9f1ceffa91%7C0%7C0%7C639305136264965933%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=62PInKwPpyGrwa3VViUOFLlXisPlz4b7rgs6kdWwhNI%3D&reserved=0 	
• Fluency in English and excellent communications skills.    Applicants will also be required to meet the European Commission’s MSCA Doctoral Network eligibility criteria, notably:

   	
• Mobility Rule - Applicants can be of any nationality and must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the start of their employment at UCPH. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not considered. 	
• Doctoral Candidate requirement – the applicant must not be in possession of a doctoral degree at the first day of the employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis, but who have not yet been awarded the doctoral degree are not eligible.   Please note that you will only be considered for the position if you fulfil both above eligibility criteria.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of spatial, engineering, or behavioural sciences. Applicants can have a background in Urban and Regional Planning, Geography, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Psychology, Sociology, or related disciplines.

  The following experiences and skills will be emphasised. Applicants are encouraged to provide relevant details and supporting evidence, where applicable:

   	
• Urban design / urban planning 	
• Human-environment interactions 	
• Qualitative case study methods 	
• Data analysis / statistical analysis   Personal attributes that are desirable:

   	
• Strong motivation for high-quality research 	
• Collaborative spirit 	
• Systematic approach to research 	
• Attention to detail   Key criteria for the assessment of applicants

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevance of studies, coursework, and thesis 	
• Relevant work experience (if any) 	
• Publications (if any) 	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Other professional activities 	
• Language skills 	
• Quality and relevance of project proposal 	
• The successful applicant is also required to be enterprising and to possess good   interpersonal skills   Terms of employment
 The arrangement concerns two separate fixed-term positions: initially as a Research Assistant, leading towards an appointment as a PhD fellow. The respective durations of the two positions are 1 year and 3 years.

  The position as a PhD fellow is contingent upon the successful enrolment of a suitable candidate in the PhD School at the University of Copenhagen, as well as satisfactory completion of the Research Assistant period. These assessments will be carried out 3-6  months prior to the expiry of the Research Assistant contract. The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the faculty’s rules on achieving the degree.

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the requirements from the European Commission related to the MSCA programme and the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,850 DKK/roughly 4,260 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund. 

  Application and assessment procedure
 Your application, written in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking “Apply now” below and must include the following documents in PDF format:

   	
• Motivation letter of application (max. one page) 	
• A project proposal (max 5 pages where the candidate presents a proposal on how they wish to approach their project including theory and methods) 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills, publication list (if any), and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Certified copy of original master’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD position employment, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.
 	Applicants with a master´s degree from abroad should also enclose a short description of the grading scale used.
 	Certified copy of original bachelor’s diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If the applicant has completed a combined bachelor’s and master’s education (e.g. 5-year combined master’s), the applicant should submit the combined diploma, transcript of records, and authorised English translations if issued in other language than English or Danish. 	
• Language diplomas or language test results (if any)   The deadline for applications is 20 December 2026, at 23.59pm CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritised assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant can comment on the part of the assessment that relates to him/herself.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  You may read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  For more information on working and living in Denmark visit http://ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility) and https://www.workindenmark.dk.

  Interviews are expected to take place in the beginning of February 2027.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD position, please contact the principal supervisor, Trine Agervig Carstensen.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.
